active_experiment: ICLR 2020 T0 PDF acquisition is running under the 5-second source-respecting throttle; the offline extraction and decision-stratified missingness protocols are frozen and ready to consume completed downloads.
evidence_collected: Selective-label problem is established prior art and directly threatens naive retrospective policy evaluation.
Active learning already studies label allocation under expensive human-oracle budgets.
Published peer-review evidence does not support a blanket assumption that novelty is systematically suppressed.
Common novelty indicators are construct-sensitive and can overlap with interdisciplinarity.
Live acquisition probe returned HTTP 429 and then HTTP 403 from api.openreview.net; no corpus record was treated as acquired.
OpenReview documents supported API2 and legacy API1 retrieval for submissions, reviews, rebuttals and decisions.
Independent corpora demonstrate useful ICLR 2017-2022 coverage of submission metadata, decisions and reviews.
OpenReview-derived raw-note datasets expose note creation timestamps, but timestamps on surviving notes do not prove preservation of earlier edited states.
Historical crawler prior art explicitly models revisions of submissions and notes, providing a reconstruction lead that still requires provenance validation.
A field-by-year temporal observability matrix now separates coverage from decision-time admissibility and permits a narrower submission-time Track A without weakening review-aware Track B.
A deterministic synthetic allocation harness now tests equal-budget, no-leakage, uniqueness and reproducibility invariants without licensing empirical policy claims.
A deterministic ICLR 2020-2021 cohort manifest now freezes 5,602 records from berenslab/iclr-dataset with source hashes and independent PRRCA identity/decision witnesses.
PRRCA witness coverage is outcome-differential: 2020 accept 91.7% versus reject 77.1%; 2021 accept 91.7% versus reject 81.8%, so PRRCA cannot define the canonical candidate pool.

Cross-source reconciliation found zero decision mismatches in 2020 and one 2021 mismatch where the later berenslab snapshot is Withdrawn while PRRCA records Accept (Poster); one additional 2021 normalized-title mismatch was detected.

The full-candidate berenslab snapshots remain CURRENT_ONLY because their later scrape does not establish decision-time title/abstract/keyword state; therefore no allocator-visible field is yet T0-admissible.
ResearchArcade revision references provide 1,816 conservative pre-deadline ICLR 2020 candidates (82.1% of the ACCEPT/REJECT frame): 79.9% accepted coverage and 83.0% rejected coverage.
The same conservative pre-deadline rule yields only 195 ICLR 2021 candidates (7.5%): 6.1% accepted coverage and 8.2% rejected coverage, so 2021 is not currently suitable as a primary T0 cohort.

A deterministic 40-record retrieval probe resolved 20/20 sampled ICLR 2020 and 20/20 sampled ICLR 2021 historical revision references as HTTP 200 application/pdf; first-three-page text extraction succeeded for all 20 ICLR 2020 sampled PDFs.
OpenReview documents tmdate as a true modification date that users cannot set or modify; the T0 reference rule uses only revision tmdate values no later than the official paper submission deadline.
The frozen extraction protocol is offline and verifies each acquired PDF SHA-256 before whole-document page-order text extraction; decision labels are withheld from extraction behavior.
A 10-PDF extraction smoke test completed 10/10 with no zero-text, low-text, or page-error flags; this validates tooling only and is not empirical evidence.

A frozen outcome-blind T0 candidate representation protocol now uses only historical extracted PDF text, corpus-internal TF-IDF, deterministic truncated SVD, and transparent cosine-geometry descriptors; it explicitly forbids pretrained-model embeddings and outcome-conditioned features.

A 166-document engineering fixture produced a deterministic 128-dimensional representation; all array outputs were exactly reproducible across reruns and the row index contained none of the tested decision/review/citation strings.

A pre-outcome Track A allocation-policy protocol is now frozen across five equal-count scarcity budgets (5%, 10%, 20%, 40%, 80%) and six transparent policies: seeded random, centrality, centroid-distance, local-sparsity, greedy k-center coverage, and a 25% exploration-quota mixture.

A 166-document engineering fixture generated exact-budget selections for all policies and budgets with byte-identical selection/diagnostic/manifest outputs across reruns; no historical decision or future-value outcome was joined.

The downstream outcome definition is now frozen before policy scoring: distinct citing works in a conservative five-year post-decision window (2019-09-26 through 2024-09-25), with high-recognition defined prospectively as the matched-cohort C5 top decile.

The primary policy endpoint is frozen as high-recognition recall at the 20% attention budget, with a 5-percentage-point smallest effect of interest and a 10,000-replicate paired bootstrap precision procedure.
A network-free OpenAlex linkage query manifest can be generated for all 1,816 ICLR 2020 T0 reference candidates; the dry run made zero network calls and observed no citation outcomes.

Metadata-only OpenAlex probes showed that identical candidate papers can be represented by multiple work IDs (for example preprint and conference manifestations), so the matching protocol now freezes an exact-title+author identity-cluster rule and unions/deduplicates citing work IDs across cluster members.

The downstream evaluation engine is implemented but hard-gated: OpenAlex metadata and citation acquisition refuse to run without an explicit post-feasibility-gate flag, and both enforce provider/access controls and a configurable spend cap.
The identity resolver was validated on a synthetic fixture containing two exact-title manifestations and correctly retained both in one identity cluster without reading citation outcomes.

The frozen policy evaluator was validated only on 166 deterministic synthetic outcome fixtures; it reproduced the preregistered top-decile recall, 20% primary contrast, bootstrap precision and exchangeability-randomization machinery without touching real downstream outcomes.

The T0 technical-availability adjudication rule is now frozen before bulk acquisition completes: primary usability requires >=1000 extracted characters and zero page extraction errors; PASS requires >=95% usable retention overall and in both decision strata plus a 95% Newcombe-Wilson decision-gap interval wholly inside +/-5 percentage points.

Synthetic complete fixtures exercised all three adjudication states: PASS, CONDITIONAL and ABSTAIN. The live ICLR 2020 pipeline correctly reports INCOMPLETE_DO_NOT_ADJUDICATE while acquisition/extraction is still running.

The post-acquisition T0 finalization chain is now implemented and outcome-blind: technical adjudication -> decision-free cohort freeze -> final historical representation -> preregistered policy selections.

A 100-document complete fixture ran the entire post-gate chain end to end; the frozen cohort contained no tested decision/review/citation strings, the representation was marked FROZEN_T0_REPRESENTATION, and policy outputs were marked FROZEN_T0_POLICY_SELECTIONS.
The finalizer explicitly leaves the downstream outcome gate closed even after technical PASS/CONDITIONAL; it does not acquire or evaluate real downstream outcomes.

A pre-outcome design-precision audit is now wired into T0 finalization. It uses only frozen policy-set overlap, cohort size, the preregistered top-decile outcome fraction and the five-percentage-point smallest effect of interest; no realized citation values are required.

On the 100-document finalization fixture, all five structured-policy contrasts were prospectively precision-inadequate for a five-point recall effect, demonstrating that the audit can surface underpowered designs before outcome acquisition.

adversarial_objections: The programme's headline mechanism substantially overlaps active learning, constrained ranking and exploration/exploitation.
Citation-based outcomes are treatment-affected proxies, not counterfactual intrinsic value.
Novelty suppression is an empirical question and existing journal evidence sometimes points in the opposite direction.
A current public record is not evidence that its decision-time value is reconstructable; a temporal firewall cannot recover overwritten history.
Creation timestamps are insufficient if note contents were subsequently edited and earlier revisions are absent.
Synthetic policy results can be manufactured by scenario assumptions; Stage A is therefore an engineering test, not evidence.
